questions.q: Is Northfield Health Network, the organization in this case study, a real healthcare system?
options: No — it's explicitly described as a fictional, illustrative composite scenario
Yes — it is a real, named regional healthcare system
Yes — it is real, but with its name changed for privacy
The lesson does not say whether it is real or fictional
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly labels Northfield Health Network as fictional and illustrative, not a real organization, consistent with this catalog's policy against presenting invented scenarios as real.

questions.q: What was the root problem at Northfield Health Network, per this lesson?
options: Six hospital sites each ran Fabric independently, producing three different definitions of the same metric with an audit approaching
Northfield had no data of any kind
A single employee deleted the entire Fabric tenant
Northfield had too many certified semantic models and needed fewer
questions.explain: Six independently-run sites with no shared structure produced three competing definitions of 'Patient Readmission Rate,' with a compliance audit six weeks away.

questions.q: In the Chapter 2 step of the walkthrough, how did Research access the shared clinical data, per this lesson?
options: Through a shortcut into the same underlying data, restricted to a de-identified folder — not a separate duplicate copy
By maintaining its own fully duplicated copy of all patient data
Research was given no access to clinical data at all
Research was granted full Admin rights on the Clinical Operations domain
questions.explain: A shortcut let Research reference the same data without duplicating it, with Data Access Roles and OneLake Security narrowing it to a de-identified folder.

questions.q: Why did the compliance team's version of the readmission-rate model get Certified in Chapter 4's step, per this lesson?
options: So it was visibly the one version other people should discover and build on, instead of a seventh team rebuilding it from scratch
Certification was applied automatically with no review at all
Every semantic model at Northfield was certified, with no distinction between them
Certification was only used to restrict the model from being viewed by anyone
questions.explain: Certifying the compliance team's version, per Lesson 18, made it the discoverable, trusted source to build on rather than yet another duplicate definition.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what actually made Northfield's audit answer work six weeks later?
options: Every layer of the course — structure, security, discovery, and governed analytics — pointed at the same single source, not a last-minute rebuild
The hospital sites were merged into a single legal entity
All six workspaces were deleted and never replaced
The audit was canceled before any review took place
questions.explain: The lesson's closing point is that the fix worked because every governance layer pointed at the same certified, traceable source — not because the data was rebuilt.
